rows.jp: 帰路。

ghs.en: On the way home.

rows.jp: 大人しかった蝉たちが、再びじわじわと鳴きはじめる。
rows.en: The cicadas, quiet until then, gradually began to sing again.

ghs.en: The docile cicadas once more slowly but steadily being their cry.
ghs.assessment: The source says cicadas that had quieted down gradually begin chirping again. 'Docile' means obedient, and 'being their cry' is grammatically incoherent.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The cicadas, quiet until now, gradually begin chirping again.'

highlights.text: docile cicadas once more slowly but steadily being their cry

rows.jp: 「ちょいーす」

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "A'hoooy!"
ghs.assessment: The source is a casual contemporary greeting. The English supplies a nautical hail and changes the social flavor.
ghs.remedy: Use a casual greeting such as 'Yo.'

rows.jp: 「ん……おお、谷崎！」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Mh... oooh, Tanizaki!"

rows.jp: 「鴻巣！　元気だったか」

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Kounosu! You been in good spirits?"

rows.jp: 「ああ、この鴻巣太一、たとえ免停になっても元気だけが取り柄だ」
rows.en: “You bet. This is Taichi Konosu: even if my license is suspended, I’ve still got my health.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yup, this Kounosu Taichi here has being in spirits even in case of driving license suspension as his only redeeming feature."
ghs.assessment: The English is grammatically incoherent. The source jokes that even with his license suspended, Kounosu Taichi's only virtue is that he stays cheerful.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Even with my license suspended, staying cheerful is my one good quality.'

highlights.text: has being in spirits even in case of driving license suspension as his only redeeming feature

rows.jp: 「それを言うならこの谷崎豊だってそうだぜ？」
rows.en: “Well, this Yutaka Tanizaki can say the same!”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Ain't those the words that Tanizaki Yutaka here with his name written with the kanji for 'abundance' should be saying?"
ghs.assessment: The source says the same claim applies to Tanizaki Yutaka too. The English adds an unmarked kanji gloss and turns the parallel claim into a remark about who should say the words.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The same goes for this Tanizaki Yutaka, you know?'

highlights.text: with his name written with the kanji for 'abundance' should be saying

rows.jp: 「数日ぶりだな、谷崎」

ghs.en: Taichi: "It's been some days, hasn't it, Tanizaki."

rows.jp: 「ああ、鴻巣」

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Yah, Kounosu."

rows.jp: 「谷崎は学校いつから来んの？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "So when are you coming, Tanizaki?"
ghs.assessment: The source asks when Tanizaki will start coming to school. The English omits the destination and can sound like a question about arriving at the current place.
ghs.remedy: Use 'When are you coming to school?'

rows.jp: 「いちおー、明日になった、鴻巣」

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "'s far 's I have it, it's tomorrow, Kounosu."

rows.jp: 手にしたＡ４封筒をひらひらと振る。
rows.en: He waved an A4 envelope in one hand.

ghs.en: He waved back and forth the A4 envelope in his hands.

rows.jp: 学校関係の書類だろう。

ghs.en: Gotta be official school documents.

rows.jp: 「お、うちのクラスに転入してこいよ谷崎」
rows.en: “Hey, make sure you get put in my class, Tanizaki.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Oh, do join our class then, Tanizaki!"

rows.jp: 「鴻巣、無茶言うなよ。自分じゃ決められないってーの」
rows.en: “Don’t ask for the impossible, Konosu. I’m telling you, it’s not up to me.”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Kounosu, don't talk dumb. Ya know I can't decide that myself!"

rows.jp: 「わはは」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Wahahah!"

rows.jp: 「わはは」

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Wahahah!"

rows.jp: 二人でげはげは笑う。

ghs.en: The two of us laugh heartily.

rows.jp: 「だけどさ谷崎―――」

ghs.en: Taichi: "So, anyway, Tanizaki---"

rows.jp: 「……ＯＫギブアップだ！　新川豊です、すいませんでした黒須さん」
rows.en: “Okay, I give up! I’m Yutaka Shinkawa. Sorry about that, Mr. Kurosu.”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "...OK, it's a give-up! I'm Shinkawa Yutaka, my sincere apologies Kurosu-san!"
ghs.assessment: The source uses the direct exclamation 'I give up.' The nominal construction is an unidiomatic calque.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Okay, I give up!'

rows.jp: 「ああ、やめとく？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Aww, that's it?"

rows.jp: 「果てしなく続きそうだったから」
rows.en: “It was starting to look like we’d go on forever.”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "It's 'cause it looked like it'd have gone on forever."

rows.jp: 「もう帰り？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Going home already?"

rows.jp: 「ああ」

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Yeah."

rows.jp: 「どうする、うち寄ってくか？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "How about a trip to my house?"

rows.jp: 「近いのか？」

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Is it nearby?"

rows.jp: 「こっから十分くらいかな」

ghs.en: Taichi: "I'd say from here ten minutes are enough."
ghs.assessment: The source estimates the travel time as about ten minutes. The English treats minutes as an amount sufficient for an unstated task.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It's about ten minutes from here.'

rows.jp: 「いいトコ住んでるなぁ。けど悪い。今度にするわ」
rows.en: “Nice neighborhood. Sorry, though. I’ll take you up on it next time.”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Seems like you live in a nice place, don't you. But, sorry, some other time maybe."

rows.jp: 「姪がさー、やっぱ群青行くんだけどさ、いろいろ教えてやらんと」
rows.en: “My niece is going to Gunjo after all, so I’ve got to show her the ropes.”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Got a niece, ya know, 'course she goes to Gunjou, ya know, so she's telling me lots and lots of stuff."
ghs.assessment: The source says Shinkawa has to teach or explain various things to his niece. The English reverses the information flow and makes the niece teach him.
ghs.remedy: Use 'so I have to show her the ropes.'

highlights.text: so she's telling me lots and lots of stuff

rows.jp: 俺の耳、

ghs.en: From my ears
ghs.assessment: The source begins a subject phrase, 'My ears...' The English changes it to a source prepositional phrase that cannot govern the continuing sentence.
ghs.remedy: Use 'My ears...'

rows.jp: そういう情報、

ghs.en: information like that

rows.jp: 逃さない（ぐっ）。

ghs.en: could never run away (tahm!).
ghs.assessment: The source says his ears do not miss information like that, followed by a thumbs-up gesture. The English makes the information run away and replaces the gesture with an opaque sound.
ghs.remedy: Complete the sequence as 'would never miss information like that. (Thumbs up.)'

rows.jp: 「なに親指立ててるよ？」
rows.en: “Why are you giving me a thumbs-up?”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "What's with that raised thumb?"

rows.jp: 「ヘイ、そこのガイ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "HEI, you GUY over there."

rows.jp: 「な、なんだよ？」

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Wh, what's with that?"

rows.jp: 「マジごめん。姪、とか聞こえちゃった」
rows.en: “Sorry, man. I couldn’t help but hear ‘niece.’”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Seriously sorry. It seems I heard a word that sounded like 'niece'."
ghs.assessment: The source says he happened to hear the actual word 'niece.' The English suggests he may only have heard a similar-sounding word and adds uncertainty.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Sorry, I couldn't help overhearing "niece."'

rows.jp: 「そう言ったっちゅーねん」

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "That's what I said las' I checked."

rows.jp: 「歳は？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Age?"

rows.jp: 「俺の一個下」

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "One year younger than me."

rows.jp: 「写真持ってる？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "You carrying a picture?"
Shinkawa: "...Kurosu?"

rows.jp: 「ああ、いや、なんでもない。忘れてくれ」
rows.en: “Ah, no. Never mind. Forget I asked.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, naaah, it's nothing. Forget it."

rows.jp: 「しかしあれだ、一つ違いだと可愛いだろう」
rows.en: “Still, if she’s only a year younger, she must be cute.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But still she's gotta be cute even if there's that one thing that's off."
ghs.assessment: The source says a niece only one year younger must be cute. The English misreads the one-year age difference as a single flaw or thing that is wrong.
ghs.remedy: Use 'With only one year between you, she must be cute.'

highlights.text: even if there's that one thing that's off

rows.jp: 「んー、ま、ルックスだけはな」
rows.en: “Mm. Well, she looks good, at least.”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Hmmm, well, only the looks then."

rows.jp: 「全てじゃねぇか」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ain't they everything?"

rows.jp: 自然と声が低くなった。
rows.en: My voice dropped of its own accord.

ghs.en: My voice lowered spontaneously.

rows.jp: ある種のやっかみと嫉妬と……憎悪と。
rows.en: A certain resentment. Jealousy. And... hatred.

ghs.en: A specific envy, with jealousy... with hatred.
Shinkawa: "Huh?"

rows.jp: 「いや、気にしないで」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Nah, don't worry about it."

rows.jp: 「……つうても、ちょっと男っぽいからさ」
rows.en: “...But she’s a bit of a tomboy.”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "...if I gotta say, she looks sorta boyish I guess."

rows.jp: 「最初に言っておくと、そういう感情はないぞ。なんかそういう目で見ようとしても気色悪いだけだし」
rows.en: “Let me make this clear up front: I don’t have those kinds of feelings for her. Even trying to see her that way would just feel gross.”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "I'm telling ya this from the start, I don't feel like that about her. Lookin' at me with those eyes you got 's just creepy."
ghs.assessment: The source says Shinkawa feels gross if he himself tries to look at his niece sexually. The English instead accuses Taichi of looking at Shinkawa in a creepy way.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Even if I try to see her that way, it just feels gross.'

highlights.text: Lookin' at me with those eyes you got 's just creepy

rows.jp: 「うそダーッ！」

ghs.en: Taichi: "YOU LIEEE!"

rows.jp: 「わ、どうしたいきなり」

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Wah! What's with the sudden?"
ghs.assessment: The adjective lacks a noun and does not form an idiomatic question. The source asks why Taichi suddenly shouted.
ghs.remedy: Use 'What was that all of a sudden?'

rows.jp: 「そんなのうそだーっ！　おまえはうそつきだ！　可愛い年下の親族がいるんだぞ？　意識しないはずないじゃないか！」
rows.en: “That’s a lie! You’re a liar! You’ve got a cute younger relative—there’s no way you don’t see her that way!”

rows.jp: 「おまえは仏国書院の一冊も読まないのか！？　ありえねー！　解せねー！　よっておまえがうそつきだと証明された！」
rows.en: “Have you never read a single book from F— Press?! Impossible! Incomprehensible! Thus I have proved that you are a liar!”

rows.jp: 「黒須……かわいそうだが、マジなんだ」
rows.en: “Kurosu... I’m sorry to disappoint you, but I mean it.”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Kurosu... maybe that's lame, but I'm serious."
ghs.assessment: The source expresses pity for Taichi before insisting that the statement is true. 'Lame' instead disparages the situation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I feel sorry for you, Kurosu, but I'm serious.'

rows.jp: 「いやっ、聞きたくない！」
rows.en: “No! I don’t want to hear this!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "No! I don't wanna hear it!"

rows.jp: 「本気で、妹みたいなもんなんだよ。同居してるし」
rows.en: “Honestly, she’s like a little sister to me. We live together.”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Seriously, she's kinda like a little sister, 's all. 's just cohabitation."
ghs.assessment: The source plainly says they live together. The formal term 'cohabitation' carries an adult-partner implication that conflicts with his insistence that she is like a sister.
ghs.remedy: Use 'We live together, too.'

rows.jp: 同棲っ！？

ghs.en: Sharing the house?!
ghs.assessment: The source uses a loaded term for an unmarried couple living together, which drives the narrator's scandalized leap. The neutral paraphrase loses that implication.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Cohabiting?!' or another equivalently loaded reaction.

rows.jp: 同じベッドッ！？

ghs.en: Sharing the bed?!

rows.jp: 異性のぬくもりっ！！？？

ghs.en: The warmth of the opposite sex?!?!?!

rows.jp: 「お、おい、そのロケーションには途轍もない何者かの意志が介在しているぞ」
rows.en: “H-hey, wait. Some unfathomably powerful will is at work in that setup.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "W-, whoa, there must be the will of someone preposterous mediating in that location."
ghs.assessment: The source imagines the will of some extraordinary being intervening in the situation. The English calls the person preposterous, uses the wrong sense of 'mediate,' and reduces the situation to a location.
ghs.remedy: Use 'the will of some extraordinary being is at work in that setup.'

highlights.text: someone preposterous mediating in that location

rows.jp: 「……また都合の良い勘違いをしてるんだろうなー」
rows.en: “...You’re getting the wrong idea again because it suits you, aren’t you?”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "...another of yer convenient misunderstandings, ain't it."

rows.jp: 「そいつの家族に、俺が引き取ってもらってるんだよ」

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "That girl's family took me in and has been caring for me."

rows.jp: 「だからまあ、兄妹みたいなもんだ」

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "So it's, well, sorta like brother'n'sister 's all."

rows.jp: 「今回、家ぐるみで引っ越してきたんだよ。俺の足のこともあるけど、そいつもちょっとアレでさ」
rows.en: “The whole family moved here this time. Partly because of my leg, but she has her own... circumstances.”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Lately, they've had to move, family and all. There's this foot of mine, 'course, and she's kinda like 'that' too."
ghs.assessment: The source says the whole family moved here on this occasion. The English shifts it to an extended recent period and adds that the move was compulsory.
ghs.remedy: Use 'This time, the whole family moved here.'

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ahhh..."

rows.jp: そういうことか。

ghs.en: That's what it is then.

rows.jp: 一発で納得だ。

ghs.en: One blow and it's understood.
ghs.assessment: The source idiom means he understands immediately or from that single clue. The literal 'one blow' incorrectly evokes a physical strike.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That explains it immediately.'

rows.jp: それで二人して群青に通う、か。
rows.en: So the two of them would be attending Gunjo together.

ghs.en: That is why both of them attend Gunjou, then.

rows.jp: 「あれ、そうするとチミは、姪子ちゃんのためにつきあいで転入みたいなもの？」
rows.en: “Wait, then, my good man—are you transferring just to keep Niecey company?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ehhh, so Ol' Scratch here made a sort of a move-in for the sake of socializing with niecey-chan?"
ghs.assessment: The source asks whether Shinkawa transferred here to accompany his niece. The English invents the devilish nickname 'Ol’ Scratch' and renders the transfer and companionship relation incoherently.
ghs.remedy: Use 'So did you transfer here to accompany your niece?'

highlights.text: Ol' Scratch here made a sort of a move-in for the sake of socializing

rows.jp: 「そうなるかな。いや、俺だって障害持ちですが」
rows.en: “I suppose so. Though I do have a disability too.”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Is that it, dunno. Nah, it's 'cause I'm disabled."
ghs.assessment: The source first concedes that this is roughly true, then notes that he himself also has a disability. The English turns the concession into uncertainty and the contrast into the sole cause.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I guess that's about right. Though I'm disabled too.'

highlights.text: Is that it, dunno. Nah, it's 'cause I'm disabled

rows.jp: 「そして姪子ちゃんでもねぇけど……」

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "And don't 'niecey-chan' her, really..."

rows.jp: 「優しいお兄ちゃんだな、オイ」
rows.en: “Well, aren’t you a sweet big brother.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You are a kind-hearted onii-chan, ol' one."
ghs.assessment: The source ends with a rough attention-getter akin to 'hey' or 'man.' 'Ol’ one' is not an English form of address and suggests age without support.
ghs.remedy: Use 'You're a kind big brother, man.'

rows.jp: 「あの、姪の話になってから絡みっぱなしなんですけど？」
rows.en: “Excuse me, but you’ve been on my case without pause ever since I mentioned her.”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Uhm, didn't we kinda get all arguing since this turned to the niece?"
ghs.assessment: The source accuses Taichi alone of persistently picking at Shinkawa since the niece was mentioned. The English makes the arguing mutual and is grammatically malformed.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Haven't you been picking on me nonstop since my niece came up?'

highlights.text: didn't we kinda get all arguing since this turned to the niece

rows.jp: 「羨望を集めるってのはそういうことだ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "That is what a gathering of envy is about."
ghs.assessment: The source says that being the object of others' envy entails this treatment. The English turns envy into something that gathers and obscures the social relation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That's what happens when everyone envies you.'

rows.jp: 「そうかあ～？　ずっと暮らしてるとさー、生理的なこととか見えてきてけっこうアレなんだぜ？」
rows.en: “You think so? Live with someone long enough and you see all the bodily realities. It rather ruins the mystique.”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Is it no～w? 'Cause we've been living together a long while now, so won't I have seen how she's very much 'that', on the physical level and all that?"
ghs.assessment: The English is incoherent and uses an inappropriate future-perfect question. The source says long cohabitation exposes bodily realities that make idealization difficult.
ghs.remedy: Use 'When you've lived together this long, you see all the bodily stuff, and it can be pretty off-putting.'

highlights.text: won't I have seen how she's very much 'that', on the physical level

rows.jp: 「アレ？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "'That'?"

rows.jp: 「外見はいいとこもあるんだろうけど、欠点がバリバリ見えるから、たいしてきれいなモンにゃ思えないって感じか？」
rows.en: “She may be good-looking, but when all her flaws are right there in front of you, you don’t exactly see her as some great beauty. Something like that.”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "For the outwards she's fine for sure, but, after those weak points tear through that nice and clean, I can't really think of 'er as something pretty can I?"
ghs.assessment: The clause is incoherent. The source says her good looks are offset by glaring flaws, so he cannot see her as especially beautiful.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She may look good, but her flaws are so obvious that I can't think of her as especially beautiful.'

highlights.text: after those weak points tear through that nice and clean

rows.jp: 「食うものは食うし、出すものは―――」
rows.en: “She eats, and what she eats comes out—”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "What's for eating you eat, what's for expelling---"
ghs.assessment: The source says she eats and excretes like anyone else. The English shifts to generic second person and forms neither clause idiomatically.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She eats, and what goes in has to come—'

highlights.text: What's for eating you eat, what's for expelling

rows.jp: 「あ、その先はいいや。夢は大事にしたい」
rows.en: “That’s enough. I want to preserve the dream.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ah, that's enough with that. I wanna keep my precious dream."

rows.jp: 「……おまえの夢って」

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "...your dream you say?"

rows.jp: 「ぜひおまえとチェンジして姪子ちゃんとイチャイチャしたいものだ」
rows.en: “I’d love to trade places with you and get all lovey-dovey with Niecey.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Wanting to completely replace you and getting all kissy-kissy with your niecey-chan, of course."
ghs.assessment: The source states Taichi's wish to switch places with Shinkawa. The English is a gerund fragment, and 'completely replace you' can imply erasing the person rather than trading roles.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I'd love to trade places with you and get cozy with your niece.'

rows.jp: 「うわ－、想像させるな気持ち悪い」
rows.en: “Ugh, don’t make me picture that. Gross.”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Blaaargh, don't make me imagine that, how disgusting!"

rows.jp: 「現実は駄目だ……」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Reality is a waste..."
ghs.assessment: The source says reality is no good or unacceptable. Calling it a waste introduces a different evaluation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Reality is no good...'

rows.jp: 本気で気持ち悪がってるよ、この人。

ghs.en: This guy's really disgusted!

rows.jp: エロ小説万歳。

ghs.en: Ero LN banzai.
ghs.assessment: The source celebrates erotic novels. The English narrows novels to light novels and leaves the celebratory word untranslated as Japanese apparatus.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Long live erotic novels.'

rows.jp: 「じゃまた今度にでも遊びに来てくれ」
rows.en: “Come over and hang out sometime, then.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well, maybe sometime I'll drop in to visit if you'll have me."
ghs.assessment: The source has Taichi invite Shinkawa to visit him another time. The English reverses visitor and host, making Taichi promise to visit Shinkawa.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Come visit me sometime.'

rows.jp: 「おー、姪のことも紹介してやるよ」
rows.en: “Sure. I’ll introduce you to my niece too.”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Oh, I'll be introducing you to the niece then!"

rows.jp: 「マジか？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "You serious?"

rows.jp: 俺はわなわな震えた。
rows.en: I trembled from head to toe.

ghs.en: I shivered and quaked all over.

rows.jp: 「……たいしたもんじゃないんだけどな……あんま期待すんなよ？」
rows.en: “...There’s nothing that special about her. Don’t get your hopes up.”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "...it ain't much of a big deal so... don't expect much, will ya?"

rows.jp: たいしたものじゃない。

ghs.en: Not much of a big deal.

rows.jp: そう言ったやつの目がテポドン級の節穴であることが、後に明らかになるのである。
rows.en: It would later become clear that the man who said that had Taepodong-class holes for eyes.

ghs.en: How the guy who said this will be shown to have Taepodong-class knothole eyes will become clear afterwards.
ghs.assessment: The doubled future construction is ungrammatical and the literal 'knothole eyes' does not convey the idiom for spectacular blindness or bad judgment.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It would later become clear that his judgment was blind on a Taepodong scale.'

highlights.text: How the guy who said this will be shown to have Taepodong-class knothole eyes will become clear afterwards
